A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe HMAGAT and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-I. Corresponding content can be matched reliably; pages 3-24 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original MAPF benchmark results, component ablations, attention analyses, failure analysis, and hyperparameter sensitivity experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons in Figures 4, 8 and 9 and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same hypergraph attention architecture, three hypergraph-generation strategies, imitation-learning pipeline, quality-improvement stages, and temperature sampler.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same random/maze training environments, ten evaluation maps listed in Table 4, and handcrafted interaction scenarios. No task or environmental coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: MAGAT, MAPF-GPT variants, MAPF-GPT-DDG, SSIL, SCRIMP and DCC remain, with the same lacam3 reference (Section 4; Appendix C).

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, collision shielding, evaluation metrics, sample sizes, and map-specific step/time limits are unchanged in Sections 3.3-4 and the appendices.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Figure 5, handcrafted analyses in Section 4.3 and Appendix D, collision-shielding comparison in Appendix C, and failure, attention-dilution and sensitivity studies in Appendices G-I are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions already report averages over 128 instances and 95% confidence intervals in Figures 4, 8-9 and relevant tables. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are retained, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 reports Dense Warehouse success rates of 39.8% for HGNN and 2.3% for GNN in both versions.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, equations and reasoning are unchanged, including the HGNN updates in Section 3.1 and the assumptions and informal attention-dilution proofs in Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about group-interaction modelling, attention dilution, comparative performance, and parameter/data efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations of attention dilution and group modelling, runtime tradeoffs among hypergraph variants, and discussions of failure modes and hyperparameter robustness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-access link to the proroklab/hmagat GitHub repository. v1 referred to supplementary code in its reproducibility statement without this address. Implementation details and the existing supplementary-material description are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to pairwise models and earlier hypergraph approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The only added prose is the one-sentence code-availability footnote; the arXiv version/date stamp also changes. Scientific wording and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The new first-page footnote slightly reflows pages 1-2, moving one introduction line to page 2. Figures, tables, and the layouts of pages 3-24 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The explicit repository address makes code easier to locate than v1's reference to supplementary material, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged. Repository contents and usability cannot be verified from the PDFs.
